subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Endometrial cancer: molecular classification, systemic immunotherapy and targeted therapy

steps.tx: The **TCGA molecular classification** revolutionized endometrial oncology by replacing purely morphological subtypes with four prognostic genomic subgroups. These four categories are **POLE ultramutated**, mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR), p53-abnormal (p53abn), and no specific molecular profile (NSMP). Incorporating this genomic classification into routine pathology reporting refines risk assessment, guiding adjuvant therapy escalation or de-escalation.
steps.say: The TCGA molecular classification revolutionized endometrial oncology by replacing purely morphological subtypes with four prognostic genomic subgroups. These four categories are POLE ultramutated, mismatch repair-deficient, p53-abnormal, and no specific molecular profile. Incorporating this classification refines risk assessment.

steps.tx: The **POLE ultramutated** subgroup is characterized by pathogenic mutations within the **exonuclease domain** of DNA polymerase epsilon. These alterations disable enzymatic proofreading, generating an exceptionally elevated somatic mutational burden exceeding 100 mutations per megabase. Despite displaying high-grade histological architecture and vascular invasion, POLE-mutated tumours demonstrate an exceptionally favourable clinical prognosis with rare recurrence.

steps.tx: Frontline immunotherapy has yielded breakthrough results in advanced mismatch repair-deficient uterine cancer. In the phase 3 **RUBY trial**, adding the PD-1 inhibitor **dostarlimab** to systemic **carboplatin** and **paclitaxel** resulted in a 72% reduction in the risk of progression or death in dMMR/MSI-H advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. The remarkable durability of response establishes chemo-immunotherapy as the standard first-line treatment regimen.

In the phase 3 RUBY trial, adding the PD-1 inhibitor dostarlimab to systemic carboplatin and paclitaxel resulted in a 72% reduction in progression or death in advanced disease. The durability of response makes chemo-immunotherapy the standard treatment.

left.title: Dostarlimab + Carboplatin-Paclitaxel
points: 72% reduction in progression or death in RUBY
Profound durable disease control in dMMR

right.title: Carboplatin-Paclitaxel Alone
points: Inferior long-term plateau on survival curve

steps.tx: For patients with advanced **mismatch repair-proficient** (pMMR) tumours, targeted combination therapy provides proven survival prolongation. In the phase 3 **KEYNOTE-775** trial, combining the multi-kinase inhibitor **lenvatinib** with the PD-1 inhibitor **pembrolizumab** significantly improved progression-free and overall survival compared to chemotherapy. This combination represents the standard of care for pretreated pMMR advanced endometrial cancer.
steps.say: For patients with advanced mismatch repair-proficient tumours, targeted combination therapy provides proven survival prolongation. In the phase 3 KEYNOTE-775 trial, combining the multi-kinase inhibitor lenvatinib with the PD-1 inhibitor pembrolizumab significantly improved progression-free and overall survival compared to chemotherapy.

steps.tx: The established cytotoxic chemotherapy backbone for advanced **endometrial carcinoma** was defined by the **GOG-0209** phase 3 randomized non-inferiority trial. Systemic combination therapy with **carboplatin** target area under curve AUC 5 plus **paclitaxel** 175 mg/m2 infused intravenously every 3 weeks proved non-inferior in overall survival to three-drug TAP chemotherapy while causing substantially less neurotoxicity.
steps.say: The established cytotoxic chemotherapy backbone for advanced endometrial carcinoma was defined by the GOG-0209 phase 3 trial. Systemic combination therapy with carboplatin target area under curve 5 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 infused every 3 weeks proved non-inferior in overall survival to three-drug TAP chemotherapy while causing substantially less toxicity.

steps.tx: Adjuvant treatment for stage 3 or high-risk endometrial cancer balances local pelvis control against distant metastatic prevention. In the randomized **PORTEC-3** trial, combined adjuvant **chemoradiotherapy** consisting of external beam pelvic radiation with concurrent cisplatin followed by adjuvant carboplatin-paclitaxel significantly improved overall and failure-free survival compared to pelvic radiation therapy alone.
steps.say: Adjuvant treatment for high-risk endometrial cancer balances local pelvis control against distant metastatic prevention. In the randomized PORTEC-3 trial, combined adjuvant chemoradiotherapy consisting of pelvic radiation with concurrent chemotherapy significantly improved overall and failure-free survival compared to radiation therapy alone.

left.title: Combined Chemoradiotherapy (PORTEC-3)
points: Pelvic radiation + concurrent and adjuvant chemo
Statistically significant OS benefit in stage 3

steps.tx: **Uterine serous carcinoma** represents an aggressive subtype exhibiting ubiquitous somatic **TP53** alterations and high rates of recurrence. Approximately 30% of serous tumours display **HER2 amplification** or overexpression. Adding trastuzumab to standard carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy yields a significant progression-free and overall survival benefit in advanced HER2-positive uterine serous carcinoma, making routine HER2 testing mandatory.
steps.say: Uterine serous carcinoma represents an aggressive subtype exhibiting ubiquitous somatic TP53 alterations and high rates of recurrence. Approximately 30% of serous tumours demonstrate marked HER2 amplification. Adding trastuzumab to standard carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy yields a significant survival benefit in advanced HER2-positive disease.

rows: Hormonal therapy, chemo if high risk

steps.tx: The micrograph shows delicate **papillary fronds** lined by highly irregular cells with large dark **pleomorphic nuclei**. Nests push into nearby stroma, marking true **stromal invasion** rather than surface growth alone. The inset shows strong membrane staining, so **HER2 testing** is warranted in this serous pattern. Spotting invasion plus HER2 status matters because it confirms aggressive disease and selects patients for added targeted therapy.
steps.say: This is uterine serous carcinoma under the microscope. Delicate papillary fronds carry large irregular nuclei, and small nests invade the stroma. The inset shows HER2 membrane staining, so routine HER2 testing is needed. About a third of these tumours overexpress HER2, and positive cases gain from adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy.

steps.tx: The image shows **uterine serous carcinoma** with strong **HER2** membrane staining around glandular tumor clusters plus abnormal **p53** staining in the inset. This aggressive subtype often carries TP53 change and HER2 overexpression drives growth in a subset. Recognizing this pattern matters because HER2 positivity selects patients for added trastuzumab, improving control of advanced disease.

Spotting HER2 positivity matters because adding trastuzumab to carboplatin and paclitaxel improves outcomes in advanced HER2 positive disease, so routine HER2 testing guides treatment choice.

steps.tx: **Uterine carcinosarcoma**, previously designated as malignant mixed **Mullerian tumour**, is a true biphasic metaplastic carcinoma with sarcomatous differentiation. Because the sarcomatous elements derive clonally from the epithelial carcinoma component, management follows high-grade epithelial carcinoma paradigms. Treatment consists of surgical staging followed by systemic **carboplatin** plus **paclitaxel** chemotherapy rather than soft tissue sarcoma regimens.
